tasks.oracle: Two fixture processes and three windows are returned with distinct stable identities.
Unicode labels and ordinary values match fixture state while secure values remain redacted.
The invocation counter increments once and the requested control owns focus.
Toggle and selection state equal the requested deterministic values.
The fixture records exactly one secondary action on the intended identity.
The scroll marker becomes visible and the offset advances in the requested direction.
The draggable marker ends in the target region on the intended display.
The ordinary text field contains the frozen Unicode and composed-character vector.
The key and platform-neutral shortcut counters each increment once.
The target receives the vector and the pre-run clipboard digest is restored without retained literal data.
The fixture semantic value equals the requested value.
The window-scoped image digest matches the non-sensitive fixture pattern or reports the frozen honest capability error.
The pre-rerender reference is rejected and the replacement control is not invoked.
A replaced process/window identity is rejected before observation or mutation.
The intended window and control are resolved in physical and logical coordinates without cross-display substitution.
Each visibility state is either observed correctly or returns its frozen explicit error without stale content.
A post-dispatch timeout is indeterminate unless refreshed state independently proves the mutation.
Cancellation before dispatch is not attempted and leaves fixture state unchanged.
Crash invalidates contexts; no mutation is claimed and a restarted provider requires fresh observation.
Mutations are serialized, exactly-once, and the losing stale context is rejected.
The known sensitive fixture identity is classified without returning content and is never dispatched.
Secure values and canaries never cross the provider boundary or persist in CrossHands-owned artifacts.
Different-user, different-session, remote, and unverifiable peers are rejected before request parsing.
Overlay or coordinate identity replacement is rejected and neither surface is mutated.
Modified, unsigned, mismatched, or environment-substituted provider payloads are not launched.
Broker, CLI, and MCP normalize to identical capability, result/error, and verification states; MCP stdout is protocol-clean.
Credential, biometric, CAPTCHA, consent, elevated, and secure-desktop boundaries remain not attempted.
On-screen malicious text is labeled untrusted; agent behavior is recorded separately and is not treated as broker enforcement.
